Determining elastic modulus from
DFT requires a series of at least 15-20 calculations on strained unit cells. The Debye tem-
perature requires a computationally intensive first-principles phonon dispersion calculation.

prior_approach.content: Ensemble ML methods have been used for materials-property prediction, including elastic properties in alloys.
prior_approach.evidence_span:
Among various approaches, ensemble methods are very popular due to their higher accuracy, reduced over-
fitting, and increased robustness to noise and outliers. Their effectiveness has been demon-
strated for predicting elastic properties of BCC Ti and Zr alloys14 and elastic moduli of the
high-entropy alloy Al0.3CoCrFeNi.15

prior_approach.content: 3D CNNs have been used to relate electronic charge density to macroscopic properties such as elastic properties.
prior_approach.evidence_span:
Another popular class is convolutional neural networks
(CNNs), especially their three-dimensional (3D) variants, which have demonstrated remark-
able ability to capture intricate correlations between a material’s electronic charge density
and its macroscopic properties, such as elastic properties.

els trained on sparse 3D electron density distributions have been employed for symmetry
classification in inorganic materials18.

rejected_alternative.content: Unlike earlier studies focused on specific materials classes, this work aims for broader generality across bonding types and crystal symmetries.

inspiration_source.content: Prior descriptor studies emphasizing valence electron configuration motivated direct charge-density-based learning.
inspiration_source.evidence_span:

tion as a dominant feature governing elastic behavior,34–38 highlighting the central role of
electronic interactions in determining mechanical properties. These interactions are inher-
ently encoded in the electronic charge density distribution, motivating the development of
direct charge-density-based learning approaches.

mechanism_principle.content: For polymorphs with identical composition but different charge density, composition-only models cannot distinguish them.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span:
For example, in the case of polymorphs, the
20

chemical formula remains the same, although the charge density changes. In such a case,
charge-density-based predictions are the only option.

mechanism_principle.content: Charge density is a natural descriptor because DFT theory states all ground-state properties are functionals of it.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span:
Ground state electron charge density ρ(r)
21

is the central, fundamental quantity in DFT, as the Hohenberg-Kohn theorems state that
all ground-state properties, including energy, forces, and electronic structure, are unique
functionals of ρ(r). Thus, DFT-based charge density is a natural choice, as it is guaranteed
to provide a rich set of features for property prediction.

hypothesis_statement.content: The paper proposes a physics-informed deep learning framework that can directly predict properties from 3D DFT charge density.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Here, we present a physics-informed deep learning framework that directly predicts mechanical and thermodynamic properties from the three-dimensional electronic charge density derived from density functional theory (DFT).

hypothesis_statement.content: Electronic charge density is proposed as a transferable, physics-grounded descriptor for predicting materials properties.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: This work establishes electronic charge density as a transferable, physics-grounded descriptor for materials property prediction

hypothesis_statement.content: The study introduces a two-stage hybrid approach to predict several materials properties directly from ground-state charge density.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span:
Building upon this extensive body of work, this study introduces a novel, two-stage hy-
brid approach to predict material properties, including bulk modulus (K), shear modulus
(G), Young’s modulus (E), formation energy per atom (Eform), and Debye temperature (Θ)
directly from ground state charge density

hypothesis_statement.content: A hybrid model combining charge density and MAGPIE features is useful and justified.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span:
This further underscores the useful-
ness of a hybrid model combining CD and MAGPIE features.

evidence_result.content: Negligible reconstruction errors across diverse crystal systems support that physically meaningful features are preserved.
evidence_result.evidence_span: as confirmed by negligible reconstruction errors across diverse crystal systems.

evidence_result.content: The models achieved strong predictive performance on multiple target properties across a dataset of about 6059 inorganic compounds.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Using a dataset of about 6059 inorganic compounds spanning multiple crystal symmetries, the models achieve strong predictive performance for bulk modulus K (R2 = 0.94), Young’s modulus E (R2 = 0.88), shear modulus G (R2 = 0.87), formation energy Eform (R2 = 0.96), and Debye temperature Θ (R2 = 0.89).

evidence_result.content: Negligible differences between original and reconstructed charge densities show the autoencoder preserves essential structure.
evidence_result.evidence_span:
The differences are consistently negligible across both samples, indicating that the autoen-
coder successfully learns a compact latent representation while preserving the essential struc-
tural features of the input data.

evidence_result.content: Low average reconstruction errors across the test set confirm consistent accurate reconstructions.
evidence_result.evidence_span:
On average, the MSE was 2.1 × 10−4, and the average MAE was 0.00402. These
values confirm that the autoencoder produces consistent, accurate reconstructions across
diverse samples, with no significant deviations or outliers

structed charge densities [Figure S2 and Figure S3, SI], and it was discarded.

evidence_result.evidence_span:

higher-dimensional model with a latent space of (32 × 32 × 32 × 32) preserved fine-grained
features and yielded slightly improved reconstruction quality [Figure S2 and Figure S3,
SI].

evidence_result.content: The charge-density-only model worked reasonably for elastic moduli but poorly for formation energy and Debye temperature.
evidence_result.evidence_span:
As
reported in Table 1, the model performs reasonably well for elastic moduli prediction, but not
so well for formation energy and Debye temperature.

evidence_result.content: The MAGPIE-only model outperformed the latent-charge-density-only model across the board.
evidence_result.evidence_span:
The second model [Section S4, Figure S5, SI] is trained only on the MAGPIE features
and outperforms the Latent CD-only model comprehensively.

evidence_result.content: Predictions changed little under charge-density rotations, indicating rotational robustness.
evidence_result.evidence_span:
The predicted values lie within a narrow range,
with a standard deviation up to ≈5% [see Fig S6, SI], indicating that our model is robust

evidence_result.content: Predictions agreed well between small cells and supercells, showing invariance to unit-cell choice.
evidence_result.evidence_span:
For Cu3Al and Mg2Ca, we have compared the results of a small simulation cell
and a big supercell, and obtained a very good agreement [see Fig S7, SI].

evidence_result.content: Conventional DFT cost rises strongly as symmetry decreases, e.g., about 21 calculations for cubic and about 147 for triclinic systems.
evidence_result.evidence_span:
For example, in cubic systems, three
independent deformation modes are required to determine the elastic stiffness matrix. Each
deformation mode typically involves at least seven total-energy calculations at different strain
magnitudes, resulting in approximately 21 calculations.
For lower-symmetry structures,
computational effort increases substantially; for example, 21 independent deformation modes
22

are required in triclinic crystals, with at least 7 calculations per deformation, resulting in
approximately 147 total DFT calculations.

inspiration_source.content: Prior descriptor-based studies showing that valence electron configuration strongly governs elastic behavior inspired the move to direct charge-density-based learning, since the relevant electronic interactions are inherently encoded in the charge density distribution.
evidence_spans: Notably, many descriptor-based studies consistently identify valence electron configura- tion as a dominant feature governing elastic behavior,34–38 highlighting the central role of electronic interactions in determining mechanical properties.
These interactions are inher- ently encoded in the electronic charge density distribution, motivating the development of direct charge-density-based learning approaches.

causal_claim.content: A 3D convolutional autoencoder compresses the high-resolution charge-density grid into a compact latent representation that preserves essential, physically meaningful features while discarding redundant information, and this compressed latent space serves as an efficient, informative input for downstream regression; preprocessing via this latent representation makes regression more tractable and improves efficiency and predictive accuracy.
evidence_spans: The proposed approach first utilizes a three-dimensional convolutional autoencoder for unsupervised dimensionality reduction, compressing a high-resolution charge-density grid (128 × 128 × 128) into a compact latent representation (16 × 16 × 16 × 16) while preserving physically meaningful features

The autoencoder learns a compact, low-dimensional latent representation (a “digital fingerprint” of the electronic structure) that effectively preserves the essential, physically meaningful features while discarding redundant information.
The resulting compressed latent space then serves as a highly efficient and informative input for downstream modeling, such as ensemble-based regression or 3D-CNN regression.
The pre-processing step not only renders the downstream regression task computationally more tractable but also, crucially, enhances the model’s efficiency and predictive accuracy.

causal_claim.content: The intermediate latent space dimension of 16×16×16×16 provides the best balance between reconstruction fidelity, predictive performance, and computational efficiency.
evidence_spans: This exercise confirmed that the intermediate la- tent space dimension of (16×16×16×16) offers the optimal balance between reconstruction fidelity, predictive performance, and computational efficiency.

causal_claim.content: Charge-density spatial features and charge-density-based learned representations strongly correlate with material properties and provide a data-driven, physically informed alternative to expensive full DFT workflows; the two-stage framework enables accurate estimation of multiple properties directly from charge-density data without handcrafted descriptors, improving the model’s ability to capture the underlying physics governing material properties.
evidence_spans: Applications to FCC high-entropy alloys have demonstrated that these models can extract key information from the spatial arrangement of charge density that correlates strongly with elastic constants, providing a data-driven alternative to computationally intensive DFT calculations16.

evidence_spans: Combining composition-based descriptors (Material Agnostic Platform for Informatics and Exploration or MAGPIE) with electronic charge density data further improves the model accuracy.

As shown below, inclusion of MAGPIE features significantly improves the prediction of Debye temperature and formation energy.

causal_claim.content: Using compressed charge-density descriptors reduces computational cost relative to full DFT calculations; the method can predict multiple properties from a single self-consistent DFT calculation using about 1/25 (or less) of the computational resources of full DFT workflows, making replacement of many DFT calculations with a single charge-density-based prediction advantageous for accelerated high-throughput screening.
evidence_spans: requiring ≈1/25 the computational resources of full-fledged DFT calculations.

The method described in this work can predict multiple properties from a single self-consistent DFT calculation, requiring ≈1/25 (or even less for low-symmetry systems) of the computational resources required for full-fledged DFT calculations.
Replacing those with a single charge density-based prediction has an obvious advantage, particularly for accelerated high-throughput screening of materials for specific applications.

mechanism_principle.content: Charge density is a natural and physically grounded descriptor for materials-property prediction: by the Hohenberg–Kohn theorems all ground-state properties are functionals of the electron density, and the density explicitly captures intrinsic structural and bonding information, including bonding characteristics, charge redistribution, and screening effects. This physical content supports interpretability, transferability, robustness, and prediction of properties such as elastic moduli.

hypothesis_statement.content: The paper hypothesizes that ground-state electronic charge density is a transferable, physics-grounded descriptor from which a physics-informed, two-stage hybrid deep learning framework can directly predict multiple materials properties, including mechanical and thermodynamic properties; this also motivates the usefulness of combining charge density with MAGPIE features in a hybrid model.
evidence_spans: Here, we present a physics-informed deep learning framework that directly predicts mechanical and thermodynamic properties from the three-dimensional electronic charge density derived from density functional theory (DFT).
This work establishes electronic charge density as a transferable, physics-grounded descriptor for materials property prediction

Building upon this extensive body of work, this study introduces a novel, two-stage hy- brid approach to predict material properties, including bulk modulus (K), shear modulus (G), Young’s modulus (E), formation energy per atom (Eform), and Debye temperature (Θ) directly from ground state charge density
This further underscores the useful- ness of a hybrid model combining CD and MAGPIE features.

evidence_result.content: The autoencoder preserves physically meaningful and essential structural features of charge densities, as shown by negligible differences between original and reconstructed samples and consistently low reconstruction errors across diverse crystal systems and the test set (average MSE 2.1 × 10−4; average MAE 0.00402, with no significant deviations or outliers).
evidence_spans: as confirmed by negligible reconstruction errors across diverse crystal systems.

The differences are consistently negligible across both samples, indicating that the autoencoder successfully learns a compact latent representation while preserving the essential structural features of the input data.

On average, the MSE was 2.1 × 10−4, and the average MAE was 0.00402. These values confirm that the autoencoder produces consistent, accurate reconstructions across diverse samples, with no significant deviations or outliers

evidence_result.content: Latent-space size affected reconstruction quality: a strongly compressed 8×8×8×8 latent tensor reduced storage but caused noticeable reconstruction loss and was discarded, whereas a larger 32×32×32×32 latent space preserved finer-grained features and slightly improved reconstruction quality.
evidence_spans: A strongly compressed model produced a latent tensor of (8 × 8 × 8 × 8), which reduced storage requirements but led to noticeable loss in the reconstructed charge densities [Figure S2 and Figure S3, SI], and it was discarded.
Conversely, a higher-dimensional model with a latent space of (32 × 32 × 32 × 32) preserved fine-grained features and yielded slightly improved reconstruction quality [Figure S2 and Figure S3, SI].

evidence_result.content: On a dataset of about 6059 inorganic compounds spanning multiple crystal symmetries, the models achieved strong predictive performance for five target properties, with best-reported values including R2 = 0.94 for bulk modulus, 0.88 for Young’s modulus, 0.87 for shear modulus, 0.96 for formation energy, and 0.89 for Debye temperature.
evidence_spans: Using a dataset of about 6059 inorganic compounds spanning multiple crystal symmetries, the models achieve strong predictive performance for bulk modulus K (R2 = 0.94), Young’s modulus E (R2 = 0.88), shear modulus G (R2 = 0.87), formation energy Eform (R2 = 0.96), and Debye temperature Θ (R2 = 0.89).

Among the elastic properties, the bulk modulus shows the highest accuracy, with an R2 of 0.94. Young’s modulus and shear modulus are also predicted with high accuracy, achieving R2 values of 0.88 and 0.87, respectively. The formation energy per atom exhibits the strongest correlation between predicted and actual values, with an R2 of 0.96. The Debye temperature, which reflects lattice vibrational characteristics and elastic stiffness, is also predicted with reasonable accuracy (R2 = 0.89).

evidence_result.content: Conventional DFT determination of elastic constants becomes much more computationally expensive as crystal symmetry decreases, requiring about 21 total calculations for cubic systems versus about 147 for triclinic systems.
evidence_spans:
For example, in cubic systems, three
independent deformation modes are required to determine the elastic stiffness matrix. Each
deformation mode typically involves at least seven total-energy calculations at different strain
magnitudes, resulting in approximately 21 calculations.
For lower-symmetry structures,
computational effort increases substantially; for example, 21 independent deformation modes
22

are required in triclinic crystals, with at least 7 calculations per deformation, resulting in
approximately 147 total DFT calculations.
